title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: §14 'Relation avec jacobiennes généralisées' of the Longue Marche continuation. Let U = U_{0,3} = P^1_Z − {0,1,∞} over S_0 = Spec Z. Take its generalized Jacobian with respect to the reduced modulus 0+1+∞. This is a group scheme J* sitting in an extension 1 → J^0 → J* → Z → 1, given by the degree map. Its connected part is the rank-2 split torus J^0 = G_m^{0,1,∞}/G_m(diag), the cocharacter lattice being M = Z^3/Z·(1,1,1). There is an Abel–Jacobi morphism φ: U → J^1, where J^1 is the degree-1 component. The group S_3 = Aut(P^1, {0,1,∞}) acts on everything by functoriality, and φ is S_3-equivariant.

This page. J^1 is not only a J^0-torsor but an (S_3, J^0)-torsor, i.e. an equivariant torsor. It is therefore classified by a class in the equivariant cohomology H^1(S_0, S_3; J^0). Grothendieck claims (307): H^0(S_0, S_3; J^0) = H^1(S_0, S_3; J^0) = 0. The consequences are as follows.
- J^1 admits an S_3-invariant section.
- That section is unique, so J^1 ≅ J^0 canonically and S_3-equivariantly.
- Hence there is a canonical S_3-equivariant embedding of U_{0,3} into the torus G_m^2. This is essentially t ↦ (t, 1−t) up to signs and normalisations: the embedding underlying the abelianised fundamental group, Ẑ(1)^2 = Tate module of J^0, and dlog t, dlog(1−t).

H^0 computation. He identifies J^0 with Ker(product: G_m^3 → G_m). H^0 is then the triples of units of Z with x_0 x_1 x_∞ = 1 that are S_3-invariant, so x = x = x with x^3 = 1, forcing x = 1.

Marginal correction. The identification of the quotient G_m^3/diag with the kernel, via (x_0,x_1,x_∞) ↦ (x_1/x_∞, x_∞/x_0, x_0/x_1), is only A_3-equivariant. Transpositions act up to inversion, a sign twist. Grothendieck notes the computation is still correct here: only A_3-invariance really matters, and on ±1 inversion is trivial.

H^1 computation. This uses the Hochschild–Serre type spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(S_3, H^q(S_0, J^0)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(S_0, S_3; J^0), continued on the next page. There, Pic = 0 reduces everything to H^1(S_3, (Z^*)^3/Z^*). He then states the general vanishing (309): H^0 = H^1 = 0 for S_3 with coefficients M ⊗ I, for every abelian group I. This gives (310) for every scheme S.
errors: Notational: H^0 is written '= 0' and also computed as '= 1' (multiplicative trivial group); and 'x ∈ Z^{*{0,1,∞}}' should read 'x ∈ Z^*'.

Using Ker(G_m^3 → G_m) with the natural permutation action is not S_3-isomorphic to G_m^3/diag. The explicit isomorphism is only A_3-equivariant; for transpositions it is off by the sign character. Grothendieck flags this in the margin. Over Z it is harmless, since inversion is trivial on ±1.

The twist matters for the general claim (309) on the next page. Check: for the natural module M = Z^3/Z, H^0(S_3, M⊗I) = H^1(S_3, M⊗I) = 0 for all I. This follows from 0→I→I^3→M⊗I→0, Shapiro (H^*(S_3, I^3) = H^*(S_2, I)), and injectivity of restriction to the Sylow 2-subgroup on H^1 = I[2] and H^2 = I/2I. For the sign-twisted module, however, H^0(S_3, M⊗ε⊗F_3) ≠ 0: the class of (0,1,2) is invariant. So (309) is true only for the correct, untwisted action, which is the one coming from functoriality. The margin warning is therefore substantive.

ideas.what: Generalized Jacobian of P^1 minus three points over Spec Z with modulus 0+1+∞: J^0 = G_m^3/G_m, extension by degree, Abel–Jacobi map to J^1
ideas.modern_name: Rosenlicht–Serre generalized Jacobian; for curves of genus 0 a split torus (1-motive / Deligne's H_1 of U)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht, Serre (Groupes algébriques et corps de classes, 1959); Deligne (Théorie de Hodge III, 1-motives)

ideas.what: Classifying the S_3-equivariant torsor J^1 by equivariant cohomology H^1(S, S_3; J^0) and computing it with the spectral sequence H^p(S_3, H^q(S, J^0))
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant (Grothendieck/Hochschild–Serre) cohomology, Tohoku-style mixed group/sheaf cohomology
ideas.where_published: Sur quelques points d'algèbre homologique (Tohoku), ch. V

ideas.what: Vanishing of H^0 and H^1 of S_3 with coefficients in (Z^3/Z)⊗I, giving a unique canonical S_3-equivariant trivialisation of J^1, hence a canonical equivariant embedding U_{0,3} → G_m^2
ideas.modern_name: Canonical S_3-equivariant embedding P^1−{0,1,∞} → G_m^2 (t ↦ (t,1−t) type); abelianization of π1 of U_{0,3}

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine equivariant-cohomology computation. It shows the degree-1 component of the generalized Jacobian of U_{0,3} over Z is canonically and S_3-equivariantly trivial. The only fine point is the sign-twist warning, which is genuinely needed for the general statement on the next page. Nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The display (308) reads 'J^0 = G_m ⊗_Z M ≃ G_m^{0,1,∞}/diag ≃ Ker(G_m^{0,1,∞} → G_m)'. The target is G_m, a crossed-out label, with map (x_0,x_1,x_∞) ↦ x_0 x_1 x_∞; the crossed-out text is a crossed-out formula, not '{0,1,∞}'.

The margin note is roughly: 'Attention à l'isomorphisme donné via (x_0,x_1,x_∞) ↦ (x_1 x_∞^{-1}, x_∞ x_0^{-1}, x_0 x_1^{-1}), qui commute aux opérations de S_3^+, mais [aux transpositions seulement] à un signe près'.
In the H^0 line 'x ∈ Z^{*{0,1,∞}}', the exponent is a slip; the content is x ∈ Z^*.

The left-margin note reads approximately: 'calcul correct, car il n'y a qu'à prendre les S_3^+-invariants ... H^0(S, M_3) ... il faudrait calculer directement ... H^1(S, S_3; J^0) ≃ H^1(S_3, H^0(S, J^0)) ... H^0(S_3, H^1(S, J^0))'.
